mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising >0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by >0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds six-month average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months where HOUST exceeds the six-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month, where PAYEMS increases but UNRATE also rises, indicates labor market churning or underemployment, which reduces effective labor productivity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings behavior, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS exceeds 12-month average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month average for six consecutive months.
